I have been on a Christopher Nolan kick lately. Inception still holds up beautifully — the layered dream architecture rewards a second viewing, and Hans Zimmer's score gives every set piece an extra weight. Interstellar pushes harder on the emotional side, leaning into themes of fatherhood and time dilation in a way that earns its long runtime.

The Prestige is probably the tightest of the three; the rivalry between the two magicians is a study in obsession and the price of mastery. Outside Nolan, I rewatched The Social Network last week and was reminded how sharp Aaron Sorkin's dialogue can be. The pacing, the music, and the way ambition curdles into loneliness still feel remarkably current.
